segments.he: בזה"ל אמר רבינו ז"ל "עס איז אגרוסער סוד אין דער וועלט מען עסט" אין מע ארביט אומזיסט וסיפר ע"ז המשל וכו'.
segments.en:
In the days of Moharan'as, there was one of our fellowship who was an itinerant trader, traveling to the market fair for his livelihood. After toiling all day and returning home at night, his wife would greet him with contempt and insults as was her nature — and the home would be in disorder. Nor would there be food prepared as he wished: the floor of the entrance would be muddy and unswept, the room disordered and no food prepared — for she was a shlimazlnitze [an unfortunate, incompetent woman]. He was full of suffering from this — for he thought that at least after the toil and exhaustion of the entire day he would at least find rest at home at night — and in the end he found such "rest." He told his distress before Moharan'as — that he barely had his life from this.

Moharan'as answered him: "Who told you to imagine that when you come home you will find it bright, warm, clean, and orderly — that your wife will receive you with 'Welcome, my love and my honor' and immediately prepare the table and serve you good tasty food — and that therefore when you come home and find everything topsy-turvy you become infuriated? You are painting yourself a completely overturned picture! Rather, you should paint yourself exactly this: when you come home you will find it dark, cold, unclean, and disordered — the entrance and the room muddy — and your wife will come to meet you and curse and scold you, and you will find nothing prepared for you. Paint yourself this picture exactly. And then when you come home and look — it is still not quite as dark and not quite as cold and not as disordered as you pictured — and your wife did not receive you as badly as you imagined — and as for food, you found bread and some soup. It will already be bearable for you." And so it was.
